source.title: Generative Visual Code Mobile World Models
source.authors: Woosung Koh; Sung-Jun Han; Segyu Lee; Se-young Yun; J. Shin

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study extends power-law scaling analysis to a new setting: data-scale versus instruction accuracy for fine-tuned visual mobile GUI world models. It does not test language-model pretraining cross-entropy scaling.
record.gate_note: The directly relevant result is the reported data-size scaling analysis. The paper's broad model benchmark comparisons do not measure loss scaling. Its downstream policy experiment reports a relation between world-model performance and policy gains; this is recorded as a related finding, not as a test of the listed downstream-predictability version.
record.test_reason: The study fits power laws to its own results: instruction accuracy of a fine-tuned 8B mobile GUI world model against SFT dataset size (37K–240K) on five benchmarks. That bears on V5 in a fine-tuning setting. The test is weak: the measure is a judge-scored accuracy rather than loss, the data range spans under one order of magnitude with four points, and there is one model size.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that IAcc scales with training data following a power law (average R² 0.948). They call the trend non-saturating and project significant gains from using up to 3.7M available transitions. That projection is untested extrapolation.
record.recipe_differences: The study fits instruction-accuracy performance against fine-tuning dataset size for mobile GUI world models, rather than fitting held-out language-model pretraining loss against parameters, tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted results vary by benchmark: the reported exponents and R² values differ across the five test sets. Training data sizes tested were 37K, 77K, 129K, and 240K.

fits_no_version.finding: Across gWorld 8B, Qwen3 VL 8B and Qwen3 VL 32B, a 1.0 pp rise in world-model IAcc goes with about a 0.49 pp rise in downstream policy step accuracy (Tab. 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In mobile GUI agents, world-model accuracy predicts downstream policy gains when the world model is used as a lookahead value aid.

record.problems: The scaling analysis covers one model size, four reported training-set sizes, and five benchmarks; it measures instruction accuracy rather than held-out loss. The AitW fit has R² = 0.867, below the other four reported fits. No uncertainty intervals or error bars for the scaling fits are stated.
record.rows_left_out: The paper's model-size benchmark comparisons and detailed policy-evaluation table are not separately catalogued because they do not directly test the listed scaling versions. The aggregate downstream relation stated in § 4.8 is retained as r6.

untested.parts: Loss-based power laws; ranges spanning several orders of magnitude; parameter or compute scaling; image/video generation, repeated data, and transfer generally. Only accuracy versus SFT data size at 8B was tested.
The authors project gains up to 3.7M samples from the fit but never validate the extrapolation.
Not tested as a function of pretraining scale or loss; the 8B vs 32B gWorld comparison is two points without a fit.
Not tested; the benchmark-dependent exponents (0.074–0.166) are reported but not analysed.

missing.what: No scaling fit is reported for the KApps out-of-distribution split, although it is one of the six benchmarks; a researcher should know the fit covers five of six.
Average IAcc per dataset size across training epochs, for the in-distribution splits and for AndroidWorld. These give the raw points behind the fits.

record.verdict_notes: The paper is mainly a method paper; the scaling analysis is a small side result. The fits are in accuracy, which is bounded, so a power law cannot hold indefinitely. Small exponents over about 6.5× data are hard to tell apart from log-linear growth. The paper mentions both 240K and 260K training samples. No uncertainty is reported on the fits.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining cross-entropy versus parameter count, tokens, or compute.
Extrapolation of loss predictions from small language-model runs to much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation as a function of compute.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The study tests data-size scaling for fine-tuned visual mobile GUI world models, not image/video generation generally, repeated-data training, or fine-tuning and transfer beyond this setting.
The study relates world-model performance to downstream policy gains, but does not test downstream performance as a function of scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of exponents or compute-optimal allocations on fitting choices, and systematic bending away from a single power law.

rows.subject: gWorld 8B
rows.operation_detail: Fit instruction accuracy as a power law of training dataset size.
rows.note: The paper reports R² = 0.986 for this fit.
rows.check: Value is a fitted curve, not raw accuracies; the four underlying IAcc points per benchmark are only plotted (Fig. 5). Data range is about 6.5×, well short of several orders of magnitude.

rows.subject: gWorld 8B
rows.operation_detail: Fit instruction accuracy as a power law of training dataset size.
rows.note: The paper reports R² = 0.867 for this fit.
rows.check: Weakest fit (R²=0.867). Four points over about 6.5× data cannot separate a power law from a log-linear or saturating form.

rows.subject: gWorld 8B
rows.operation_detail: Fit instruction accuracy as a power law of training dataset size.
rows.note: The paper reports R² = 0.978 for this fit.
rows.check: Same caveats as r1: fitted curve only, about 6.5× data range.

rows.subject: gWorld 8B
rows.operation_detail: Fit instruction accuracy as a power law of training dataset size.
rows.note: The paper reports R² = 0.960 for this fit.
rows.check: Same caveats as r1. Benchmark name is GUIOdyssey; the paper's figure spells it 'GUIOddyssey'.

rows.subject: gWorld 8B
rows.operation_detail: Fit instruction accuracy as a power law of training dataset size.
rows.note: The paper reports R² = 0.948 for this fit.
rows.check: Same caveats as r1. AndroidWorld is an out-of-distribution split.

rows.subject: gWorld 8B, Qwen3 VL 8B, and Qwen3 VL 32B (aggregate stated by authors)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate downstream mobile GUI policy performance using world models.
rows.measure: Change in downstream policy performance associated with world-model performance
rows.value: On average, a 1.0 percentage point increase in world modeling performance translates to a 0.49 percentage point improvement in downstream policy.
rows.note: This is the authors' aggregate statement across gWorld 8B, Qwen3 VL 8B, and Qwen3 VL 32B; it is not a result linking downstream performance to scale or pretraining loss.
rows.check: Relates world-model accuracy to downstream policy gain across three different models. Not a scale or loss relation, so correctly kept as a non-version finding.

relationships.condition: gWorld 8B (Qwen3 VL 8B SFT), IAcc versus SFT data size 37K–240K, on AndroidControl, AitW, AMEX, GUIOdyssey and AndroidWorld
relationships.reason: Power-law fits with R² 0.867–0.986 and monotonic gains (r1–r5). The evidence is narrow: four points over under one order of magnitude, with an accuracy metric rather than loss.
relationships.display_finding: IAcc improves monotonically with power-law fits achieving R² = 0.867–0.986 across four data sizes spanning less than one decade.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
